text:
Henry Cho: hey all — want to align PM expectations for the SDK parity launch notes + customer messaging + success metrics. trying to avoid "this might break you" vibes but still be clear about behavior changes (retries/timeouts/streaming). can folks drop what they think we should say + how we measure success?

Monica Patel: yep. key framing from DevEx: this is primarily "more predictable / consistent" across Python/TS/Go. we should call out that defaults are changing in a couple spots (timeouts + retryable cases), but we’ve tried to keep it non-breaking and have migration notes.

Elliot Price: +1. from docs standpoint, we should point people at one canonical migration guide and avoid duplicating details in release notes. release notes should be short + link out.

Wei Chen: draft messaging suggestion:
- what: "SDKs now share consistent auth resolution, retry/backoff, timeout model, and streaming disconnect behavior"
- why: "reduces intermittent failures + ‘works in TS but not Python’ issues"
- action: "upgrade to X.Y, review migration notes if you customized retries/timeouts"
- reassurance: "no API surface redesign; existing API keys still work"

Connor O'Brien: for launch notes, can we get explicit version targets per SDK? we need a coordinated publish window or we’ll confuse ppl (Python says one thing, TS another).

Talia Benson: timeline check — we’re aiming beta in week 6, stable in week 8 per plan. would recommend: 1) beta announcement to a small set (internal + a few customers), 2) stable announcement once conformance suite green across all three.

Dev Patel: from support POV, biggest pain is customers not seeing request_id and not understanding whether they should retry (esp streaming). launch notes should explicitly say: "Errors include request_id" + "Retry-After respected on 429" + "Streaming retries are conservative; see guidance."

Allison Grant: metrics we should commit to (and mention internally, maybe not all customer-facing):
- support tickets tagged sdk-retry/sdk-timeout down (baseline last 30d)
- client-side retry rate (per request) doesn’t spike unexpectedly post-launch
- 429 follow-on load (retry storm risk) stays within bounds
- timeout error rate goes down for default configs
- streaming disconnect reasons: track % of disconnects that surface a typed error w/ request_id

Henry Cho: super helpful. re: customer-facing success metric… maybe we just say "reduced intermittent failures" + "clearer observability" rather than quoting numbers.

Ibrahim Khan: on what changed (for accuracy):
- retry policy: 429 + selected 5xx + transient network errors; exponential backoff w/ jitter; respect Retry-After (seconds + date)
- timeout model: consistent across SDKs; streaming uses overall timeout semantics differently than non-streaming but now documented
- error taxonomy: typed errors w/ status_code, request_id, retryable bool
- streaming: if disconnect mid-stream, we surface partial output + a terminal error; we do NOT auto-retry streaming by default

Monica Patel: also auth resolution order got normalized. we should be explicit about env var precedence and that we’re deprecating a couple old env var names (with warnings).

Wei Chen: re: wording on streaming — suggest:
"If a streaming connection drops, the SDK raises a typed StreamingDisconnected error and includes any partial tokens already received. Because re-sending a stream can duplicate side effects, the SDK does not automatically retry streams. See docs for safe retry patterns and idempotency guidance."

Elliot Price: docs links we should reference:
- migration notes (auth/retry/timeout): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEX/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout
- streaming guide parity update: (docs PR has final URL once merged)
We should keep release notes to ~5-8 bullets, then link.

Connor O'Brien: release mechanics proposal:
- all three SDKs ship same week w/ consistent changelog section heading: "SDK Standardization (Auth, Retries, Timeouts, Streaming)"
- same snippet in each repo + link to central migration doc
- announce in #announcements + docs site post

Dev Patel: + add a support macro update. if we can tell customers "please share request_id + sdk version + retry config" we’ll cut time-to-triage.

Allison Grant: +1. also want to ensure we’re not overpromising on retries. SRE concern is thundering herd. so we should avoid "automatic retries fix everything" language.

Henry Cho: ok. draft customer-facing release note bullets (tell me if anything is wrong):
1) Consistent auth configuration and env var precedence across Python/TS/Go
2) Standard retry policy (429/5xx/transient network) w/ exponential backoff + jitter; respects Retry-After
3) Standard timeout model + clearer streaming vs non-streaming behavior
4) Improved error typing + request_id surfaced for faster debugging
5) Streaming disconnects surface partial output + typed error; guidance for safe retries/idempotency

Monica Patel: looks right. slight tweak: call out "retry policy is configurable" and defaults are tuned to avoid retry storms.

Ibrahim Khan: and for migration note callout: "If you previously relied on unlimited/implicit retries or custom timeout defaults, review config options." (TS had some weird defaults historically.)

Wei Chen: I’ll update migration doc intro to match this framing and add a “What you need to do / What you don’t need to do” section. customers love that.

Talia Benson: can we lock “definition of done” for launch?
- conformance suite passing across all three
- docs merged + published
- support macro updated
- observability dashboard live for rollout monitoring

Allison Grant: + rollout triggers/rollback thresholds (internal): if retry rate > X% sustained or 429 amplification > Y, we pause.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll sync with release channel on version numbers once we confirm final tags. we should avoid shipping one SDK as stable while another still in beta.

Henry Cho: perfect. action items:
- Wei/Elliot: finalize customer-facing wording + migration doc intro
- Connor/Talia: coordinated release plan + version targets
- Allison: finalize success metrics + dashboards for week-8 monitoring
- Dev: support macro + what we ask customers for
I’ll own the final announcement draft once we have URLs. :thumbsup:

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: will loop Owen in for support macro review.

Wei Chen: ack. will post draft blurb here later today.

Monica Patel: thanks all — keeping this crisp is key. we’ll make sure the announcement reads like "quality of life" not "breaking change".
